incident-bot: [P1] Redwood Dedicated EU-west: sustained capacity saturation impacting enterprise reserved pools (auto-escalation)
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert -> P1: dedicated-eu-west-gpu-pool saturated (queue growth, 429s on reserved routes). Triggered at 2024-11-20T09:20:34Z
sophie (oncall): I’m on it. Paging eng-sre. First check: are autoscale policies triggering? Anyone already started the scale job?
misha (eng-sre): looking. Autoscaler shows burstEnabled=true but we’re hitting a hard quota on the shared host group. Scaling attempts are queuing with AWS error: "InsufficientInstanceCapacity". Collecting affected routes now.
sophie (oncall): priority: 1) mitigate customer impact for reserved customers, 2) update status page, 3) notify affected AEs/CS. Misha, what’s the customer list on reserved routes showing errors?
misha (eng-sre): short list from logs (top offending routes):
```
lumina-care-prod
lumina-care-analytics
argo-insurance-dedicated
helix-bio-dedicated
```
These are returning 429 or timing out at ~1.2s higher p50 to failure.
kevin (customer-success): LuminaCare is in our enterprise SLA. Donna — I’m pre-drafting a tailored customer notification. Need exact impact description and recommended workarounds (if any).
kevin (customer-success): Donna / account execs: please confirm the primary on-call contacts for LuminaCare and Argo.
donna (acct-exec): LuminaCare contacts: @lumina-prod-ops (ops@luminacare.com), escalation to CTO Kate Lin. Argo primary: eng-lead@argo-ins.com, CC: PM Samir Patel. I’ll loop them after we confirm messaging.
tanya (prod-ops): quick mitigation idea: route reserved traffic for those accounts to the compatible non-dedicated region (hosted tier) as temporary fallback. Requires opt-in policies we already have for enterprise fallbacks. Risk: higher per-token cost and potential data residency concerns for EU.
oliver (legal): note on data residency — if we route to hosted non-EU, we need LuminaCare approval. Donna, confirm whether contract allows cross-region fallback under emergency.
sophie (oncall): Misha, can we do a soft-failover: for lumina-care-prod route, send 10% traffic to fallback-hosted-eu (same region if available) and keep 90% queued? That buys us time while autoscaling retries.
misha (eng-sre): I can flip a canary route now. Executing route update: `rwctl route update --route lumina-care-prod --fallback hosted-eu-canary --weight 10` — applying.
statuspage-bot: Status page update queued: "Investigating: Dedicated EU-west capacity issue causing errors and elevated latency for some enterprise customers." Draft published to private incidents page.
sophie (oncall): Drafting status page and customer-facing lines. Posting here for review before public/internal send.

--- STATUS PAGE / CUSTOMER-FACING DRAFT ---
Status: Investigating
Impacted: Dedicated EU-west reserved capacity for a subset of enterprise customers (examples: lumina-care-prod, argo-insurance-dedicated).
What’s happening: We have detected sustained saturation in our Dedicated EU-west GPU pools causing increased request queueing and intermittent 429s for affected reserved routes. Our on-call team is activating mitigations (canary fallback and capacity requests) and working with cloud infra to procure additional capacity.
Customer guidance: If you experience request errors (429) or elevated latency, please retry after a short backoff. Customers on enterprise contracts may see temporary routing to a fallback hosted endpoint under emergency fallback policy. We will not change data handling without prior agreement for cross-region fallback — customer success will contact affected customers directly.
ETA for next update: 15 minutes.
--- END STATUS PAGE ---
